TAX SOURCES · FIXED AND HOURLY

Which tax applies to each plan?

PER kWh · NOT A SUPPLY PERCENTAGE

ComEd states that taxes and fees use the same rates on fixed and hourly pricing. The Illinois residential excise tax is based on monthly household kWh, not the electricity supply price. ComEd billing FAQ · Illinois tax rule §511.110

State tax rules and independently entered local-tax scenarios for each supply plan.
Tax treatmentFixed pricingHourly pricing

State and default Glenview amounts are the added household tax from EV charging: tax with EV kWh minus tax without EV kWh. Glenview’s filed schedule starts at 0.556¢/kWh for the first 2,000 monthly kWh and 0.366¢/kWh for the next 48,000, confirmed in the 2024, 2025, and 2026 filings. The current sheet is effective October 1, 2026. Its 3% collection compensation is already included. The same schedule in 2022–2023 is a flagged historical assumption. Different entered overrides do not establish different legal rates. 2026 ComEd Rider TAX · Glenview, sheet 261 · 2025 Rider TAX filing

How the simulation works

Actual daily energy, assumed hours. The trace contains daily home kWh, not connection timestamps. Each positive day is modeled independently from 8 p.m. to 8 a.m. at the selected power. Home kWh is used directly, with no added charging-loss factor. Supercharger and other-location energy are excluded.

Prices available at the time. SPARC schedules using the supplied day-ahead forecasts, with a modeled 5 p.m. publication on the preceding day. Final cost uses each hour’s average of all twelve five-minute readings. Incomplete prices and infeasible energy targets are excluded from every option.

Itemized bill components. Supply, fixed-plan purchased electricity adjustments, transmission, distribution, state distribution charge, and the supplied riders are applied using the charging month. State excise tax is the incremental household tax after adding the EV’s monthly energy. This uses calendar months and an assumed household base; actual billing-cycle dates are unavailable.

Monthly charges. Customer, metering, low-income recovery, and hourly-plan capacity charges are allocated by the EV’s share of modeled total household kWh. This is an accounting assumption, not a claim that EV charging causes those entire fees.

Data limits. Historical rate assumptions and backfills are preserved. Glenview’s municipal tax tiers are confirmed in 2024–2026 filings and apply by default to this confirmed Glenview address; their use in 2022–2023 is an assumption. Optional per-plan overrides are user scenarios, not a sourced difference between supply plans. Chicago-only taxes are not applied. Franchise adjustments and unavailable hourly-specific charges are excluded.
